candidates.phrase: God, by grace, has forgiven our sins because of Christ’s blood poured out for us
candidates.rationale: The catechism states directly that God, by grace, has forgiven our sins, predicating forgiveness of God himself and asserting remission of sin.
candidates.chunk_text: Q. What does it mean to be washed with Christ’s blood and Spirit? A. To be washed with Christ’s blood means that God, by grace, has forgiven our sins because of Christ’s blood poured out for us in his sacrifice on the cross. To be washed with Christ’s Spirit means that the Holy Spirit has renewed and sanctified us to be members of Christ, so that more and more we become dead to sin and live holy and blameless lives.

candidates.phrase: God, because of Christ’s satisfaction, will no longer remember any of my sins
candidates.rationale: The catechism has God himself declare he will no longer remember the believer’s sins, asserting remission of sin as God’s own act.
candidates.chunk_text: Q. What do you believe concerning “the forgiveness of sins”? A. I believe that God, because of Christ’s satisfaction, will no longer remember any of my sins or my sinful nature which I need to struggle against all my life. Rather, by grace God grants me the righteousness of Christ to free me forever from judgment.

candidates.phrase: he forgives all sinners of all sins except the one sin against the Holy Spirit
candidates.rationale: After denying that grace excuses sin, the confession positively teaches that he (God) forgives all sinners of all sins except blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.
candidates.chunk_text: ERRORS. Wherefore we condemn all impious utterances of some who wrongly use the preaching of the Gospel and say that it is easy to return to God. Christ has atoned for all sins. Forgiveness of sins is easy. Therefore, what harm is there in sinning? Nor need we be greatly concerned about repentance, etc. Notwithstanding we always teach that an access to God is open to all sinners, and that he forgives all sinners of all sins except the one sin against the Holy Spirit (Mark 3:29).
